context.title: A Painful Covenant
context.summary: Moved by Ezra's prayer, the people agree to send away their foreign wives. An assembly meets in the cold winter rain, and over three months the leaders examine each case. The book ends with a list of those involved.
context.background: The assembly met in the ninth month (about December), in the rainy season (vv. 9, 13). Four men opposed the plan (v. 15). The book closes abruptly on a sobering note: 'some of them had wives by whom they had children' (v. 44).

customs.note: Anyone who ignored the summons would have property confiscated and be excluded from the community.
A handshake that sealed a pledge.

people.name: Ezra
people.summary: The “scribe” who led the second body of exiles that returned from Babylon to Jerusalem B.C. 459, and author of the book of Scripture which bears his name.

people.name: Shechaniah
people.summary: The father of Shemaiah, who repaired the wall of Jerusalem (Neh. 3:29).

people.name: Benjamin
people.summary: The younger son of Jacob by Rachel (Gen. 35:18). His birth took place at Ephrath, on the road between Bethel and Bethlehem, at a short distance from the latter place.

people.name: Jonathan
people.summary: Jonathan is a heroic figure in 1 Samuel in the Hebrew Bible. A prince of the United Kingdom of Israel, he was the eldest son of King Saul as well as a close friend of David, who eventually succeeded Saul as king.

people.name: Shabbethai
people.summary: Sabbath-born, a Levite who assisted in expounding the law and investigating into the illegal marriages of the Jews.

people.name: Jeshua
people.summary: Head of the ninth priestly order (Ezra 2:36); called also Jeshuah (1 Chr. 24:11).

people.name: Eliezer
people.summary: Descendant of Joshua son of Jozadak.

people.name: Maaseiah
people.summary: The priest who divorced his wife.

people.name: Immer
people.summary: The head of the sixteenth priestly order (1 Chr. 24:14).

people.name: Harim
people.summary: The head of the second course of priests (1 Chr. 24:8).

people.name: Eliashib
people.summary: The High Priest is mentioned in Nehemiah.

people.name: Benaiah
people.summary: Son of Jehoiada, fighter from Kabzeel.

people.name: Jeremoth
people.summary: One of the sons of Elam.

people.name: Zattu
people.summary: Id., one whose descendants returned from the Captivity with Zerubbabel (Ezra 2:8; Neh. 7:13); probably the same as Zatthu.

people.name: Adaiah
people.summary: Adaiah son of Jeroham, the son of Pashhur, the son of Malkijah; and Maasai son of Adiel, the son of Jahzerah, the son of Meshullam, the son of Meshillemith, the son of Immer.

people.name: Pahath-moab
people.summary: Governor of Moab, a person whose descendants returned from the Captivity and assisted in rebuilding Jerusalem (Ezra 2:6; 8:4; 10:30).

people.name: Benaiah
people.summary: Benaiah in the Bible is the son of Jehoiada, who came from the southern Judean town of Kabzeel.Benaiah was one of King David’s mighty men, commander of the 11th rotational army division; a Pirathonite of the tribe of Ephraim. He helped David's son Solomon become king, killed Solomon's enemies, and served as the chief of Solomon's army. On Solomon's instructions he was responsible for the deaths of Adonijah, Joab and Shimei. He was in charge of the Cherethites and Pelethites. Several verses in 1 Kings 1 make clear that Benaiah was closely associated with Solomon's party and excluded from Adonijah's faction.

people.name: Benaiah
people.summary: Commander of the Cherethites and Pelethites.

people.name: Eliashib
people.summary: A high priest in the days of Nehemiah.

places.name: Jerusalem
places.summary: Called also Salem, Ariel, Jebus, the “city of God,” the “holy city;” by the modern Arabs el-Khuds, meaning “the holy;” once “the city of Judah” (2 Chr. 25:28).

places.name: Nebo
places.summary: The “children of Nebo” (Ezra 2:29; Neh. 7:33) were of those who returned from Babylon.
